mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% is followed by positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of instances, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL YoY and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS drops > 100k in a month and is followed by positive 5-day forward returns in > 60% of instances, or if the correlation between PAYEMS changes and 5-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases are not followed by positive 60-day forward returns in > 55% of instances, or if the correlation between HOUST and 60-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO drops > 1% MoM and is followed by positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of instances, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 2.5% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4%, it signals a tightening monetary policy in a strong labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening cycle in strong labor market
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4% is followed by positive 20-day forward returns in > 60% of instances, or if the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and UNRATE on 20-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in three months signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises > 0.5% in 3 months and is followed by positive 60-day forward returns in > 60% of instances, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by less than 1% quarter-over-quarter and consumer sentiment (proxied by RSAFS) drops by more than 5%, it signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 < 1% QoQ and RSAFS drops > 5% is followed by positive 60-day forward returns in > 60% of instances, or if the joint effect of GDPC1 and RSAFS on 60-day forward returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS drops > 0.25% in a month and is followed by negative 5-day forward returns in > 40% of instances, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS changes and 5-day forward returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
